steps.note: S1.1.1.1.1 states that the first two rows subtract Ja+Rc, the middle rows add R(c+Gx)+J(a+Vx) and the last rows restore a,c, so the net target change (JV+RG)x is independent of a,c, as at lines 744-750.

S1.1.1.1.2 gives the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, the side wires cancelling exactly the intersection-one pairs, zero for distinct triples meeting in zero or two points, and self coefficient 3=1, matching lines 752-755.
The plan treats only the bit case of the exchange; the complex-case central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2 and the side wires' cancellation of intersections zero and two appear nowhere.
S1.1.1.1.3 states the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), each invocation restoring its own auxiliary wires, as at lines 761-764.

The plan asserts that every edge joins nested labels (S1.1.1.3, S1.1.1.3.4) and gives the residuals of the center 3->4 and side 2->5 edges only; it never states the per-edge residual table with its dimensions.

S1.1.1.3.3 states the side-edge inclusion (B⊗F)⊥(P⊗<t_X>) ⊂ (B⊗F)⊥(P⊗t_Y^⊥) and that it holds because t_X⊥t_Y, but it omits the complement <t_X,t_Y>^⊥ of dimension h-2 that the sub-step defines; unsure, so marked absent.

S1.1.1.3.4 makes center 3->4 (removing P⊗F⊗Q, dimension h) the only decreasing edge, and S1.1.1.3.5 telescopes to sinks Wm-N minus sources N, so Wm-2N, with absolute changes adding 2L, as at lines 1061-1071.

S2.1.1.1 states that each nonzero binary residual is nondegenerate, contains a norm-one vector and so is nonalternating, and has an orthonormal basis by splitting off unit lines and absorbing alternating planes, as at lines 1073-1102.
S1.1.1.3.6 gives L_b/N=100/539 and S2.1.1.4 gives L_c/N=101/539, matching lines 1105-1109.

S2.1.1.2 states that orthogonal binary vectors have supports meeting evenly, so weight is additive mod 4, and that q_V-q_U equals the sum of wt(v)[v·x] over an orthonormal basis of the residual, as at lines 1232-1245.

S2.1.1.3 states that wt(v) is odd, writes i^{±[v·x]} as (1+i^{±1})/2+(1-i^{±1})/2(-1)^{v·x}, and has conjugation by H^{⊗m} turn it into aI+bX_v or its inverse; this faithfully paraphrases the H diag(1,-1) H = X step.
The plan counts the kernels as s_c per network (S2.1.1, S2.1.1.4) but never states that on k columns each residual vector contributes one tensored factor (C_V C_U^{-1})^{⊗k} = Π K_{e,v}^{⊗k}.

S2.1.1.5 gives frame I for zero labels and C^{⊗m} for full labels, C^{-1} on the 27 support coordinates of u_a, and its repair by Z signs before and after with the scalar i^{27k}; the identity appears as C^{-1}=-iZCZ in S2.1.2's method, and the negation of the X outputs only as 'undoing of the signed bank exchange' in S2.1.2.2.
S1.1.1.4.3 states s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b, short of W_b m by N-2L_b>0 because L_b/N<1/2, and S1.1.1.3.6 quotes line 1110 that the ratios are below 1/2.
The value eta_c=73/19906842167500 appears nowhere in the plan; the complex deficit is given only as 2N-2L_c>0 (S2.1.1.4).

S1.1.4.3 gives the chain: deficit above 20·2^{-50}, log m<20, so m^{1-2^{-50}} > m(1-20·2^{-50}) > m(1-eta_b) = s_b/W_b, quoting line 1331 on both deficits, and S5.1.1 fixes tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}; the chain is spelled out for the bit network only.

S1.1.2.1 states the elimination: pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost nonzero entry, clearing by lower-triangular row and column operations, one rank-one block per pivot, so Pi has exactly a ones (A=0 handled), as at lines 1375-1391.

S1.1.2.2 states choosing once a fixed odd prime avoiding every denominator and diagonal numerator in the finite table, so the identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors, as at lines 1413-1423.
S1.1.2.3 states that a lower-triangular change costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order from still-original earlier coordinates, as at lines 1425-1430.
S1.1.2.4 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, an interchange, D_j<-H_i-D_j yielding (h+d,d) for each one of Pi, and S1.1.2.5 gives one interchange each, a in all, as at lines 1432-1446.
S2.5.1 and S2.5 give E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E and Delta=ceil(C_0 d^20), but never define nu, C_0=128mB^2 or C_1=max{20,nu+3}, nor state nu=11 and C_1=20, so the constants are only partly stated.
S2.5.1 states a gain of at most E per network invocation and at most 8e at a leaf, with the recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, matching lines 2514-2518.
S2.5.1 states the unrolled bound 8dB^{k+1}<=8B^2 d^{nu+1} (quoting line 2534) and the total of at most C_0 d^20 with the outer phases and scale, as at lines 2523-2560.

S2.5.2 states that depth-j values lie in 2^{-(p+j)}Z[i] with modulus at most 2^j, so p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits are exact, and S2.5.3 derives Delta=o(p) from 20·epsilon<1 (quoting epsilon·C_1<1), as at lines 2562-2586.
S2.5.4 states that every row of the layer has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved and the final truncation errs by less than sqrt2·2^{-p}, quoting line 2751.

summary: P03 states 20 of the 26 sub-steps. It carries the scratch-restoring exchange (bit case), the telescoping label budget, the binary orthonormal bases, the phase-frame factorization and endpoint repair, the bit-network deficit, all four matrix-shear steps, and the depth recurrence and precision steps of the simultaneous layer. It omits the complex-case exchange coefficients (B3), the per-edge residual table (L1), the h-2 complement of the side edge 2->5 (L2), the tensoring over k columns (P3), eta_c (R3), and the full constant definitions nu, C_0, C_1 (S1).
